scenes.title: Up on the Balcony
scenes.summary: On Friday morning, M1, M3, and F1 step onto the sunny second-floor courtyard balcony and test the original iron hooks made for festival lantern cords.
scenes.intro: Bright Friday morning sunshine fills the upper courtyard balcony of {SHOW}. {M1} taps each heavy timber post with his palm while {M3} checks measurements in his leather notebook and {F1} holds a basket of folded paper lanterns. Listen first.
story: F1
What a view from up here—you can see the whole courtyard tree and {STREET}!
M1
Solid seasoned oak along this entire railing; not a single loose bolt anywhere.
M3
Look at these four iron rings along the beam—spaced exactly two metres apart.
F1
So thirty summers ago, they really hung four golden lines down toward the courtyard tree!
M1
Feel how smooth the inside of this iron ring is from old hemp rope, {M3}.
M3
If we angle two lines left and two lines right, every table gets warm light.
F1
How high above {M2} and his head will the lowest lantern hang, {M3}?
M3
Three full metres clear—even if {M2} jumps for joy, his glasses are safe!
M1
Speaking of the boss, why has he stayed inside Room Nine since eight this morning?
F1
He bought a giant roll of white poster paper and a bottle of blue ink!
M3
Uh-oh—is he drawing an official anniversary seating chart for twenty-eight guests?
M1
Mark my words, {F1}: loose poster paper and Friday wind never end quietly.
scenes.outro: The upper balcony rings are rock solid, while downstairs in Room 9 {M2} is busy creating a giant paper masterpiece. See you next time.

scenes.title: Stringing Gold Above the Tree
scenes.summary: M3 and M4 stretch warm gold-and-coral lantern cords from the upper balcony to the courtyard shade tree while F2 directs the symmetry from below.
scenes.intro: At eleven o'clock, {M4} joins {M3} on the upper balcony to pass braided lantern cord down toward the courtyard tree, while {F2} stands beside the stone basin below shielding her eyes and calling directions. Let us listen in first.
story: M4
Easy on the left cord, little brother—raise your side about ten centimetres higher!
F2
Hold it right there, both of you! From the kitchen door, that curve looks magical!
M3
How many paper lanterns can we clip along each span without weighing the cord down?
M4
Six round lanterns per line makes twenty-four glowing moons above the tables!
F2
Alternate warm gold and soft coral so the whole stone courtyard feels like sunset!
M3
Catch the end of line three down by the lower tree branch, {F2}!
F2
Caught cleanly! Tell me what kind of knot keeps this cord tight until tomorrow night!
M4
Wrap twice around the iron ring and pull a double hitch—Grandfather taught us both!
M3
Look at the leaves rustling at the top of the tree; the breeze is waking up.
F2
Do you feel that cool gust coming through the street arch just now?
M4
Better wait to unfold the delicate paper globes until we test the afternoon wind?
F2
Too late—{M2} already unfolded twelve lanterns on line one AND he is marching out!
scenes.outro: Twenty-four lantern hooks span the sky above the courtyard, right as the afternoon breeze picks up speed! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Master Seating Chart
scenes.summary: Inside Room 9, M2 proudly shows F1 and F3 his enormous hand-lettered seating poster for twenty-eight guests and refuses to make a backup copy.
scenes.intro: Moments before stepping outside, inside quiet Room 9, {M2} holds up a one-metre sheet of crisp white poster paper covered in flourishing blue ink names while {F1} and {F3} admire his calligraphy. Listen first.
story: M2
Three hours of work, ladies—behold the Official Thirtieth Anniversary Courtyard Seating Plan!
F3
My goodness, {M2}, your blue fountain-pen lettering looks like a royal concert programme!
F1
Table One under the tree for our Room Eight mapmaker, {F3}, and number ten!
M2
Every neighbour from {STREET} sits beside someone who shares their favourite tea or hobby!
F1
Let me copy those twenty-eight seat numbers into the heavy paper ledger right now, {M2}.
M2
Copy it? Why hide a work of art inside a dusty pencil notebook, {F1}?
F3
Fountain-pen ink does run rather quickly if even two drops of water touch it, {M2}.
M2
There is not a single raincloud in {CITY} today, {F3}—pure golden sunshine!
F1
Yes, sunshine plus strong Friday wind whistling down {STREET} right outside the gate!
M2
I shall carry this poster firmly in both hands straight to the wooden easel outside.
F3
At least slide your reading glasses onto your nose before you cross the threshold!
M2
Watch and learn—nothing could possibly happen between Room Nine and table one!
scenes.outro: Famous last words in bright blue fountain ink as {M2} carries his giant uncopied chart toward a windy doorway! See you next time.

scenes.title: A Sudden Gust of Wind
scenes.summary: Stepping into the courtyard, a sudden wind gust tangles the overhead lanterns and launches M2's giant seating chart straight across the stones.
scenes.intro: The instant {M2} steps into the open courtyard with his giant white poster, a lively afternoon wind sweeps straight through the front gate. {F1} and {M4} sprint across the flagstones to help. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M2
Whoa! Why is my seating chart pulling like a sailboat on the open sea?!
F1
Hold both bottom corners tight, {M2}—a huge gust just came through the arch!
M4
Look up! Line one of the paper lanterns is spinning around line two!
M2
Oh no, my glasses are slipping off my forehead—let me grab them with one hand!
F1
{M2}, DO NOT LET GO OF THE RIGHT CORNER OF THE PAPER!
M2
WHOOSH! Come back here, Tables One through Seven! Stop flying toward the tree!
M4
I almost caught it by the herb pots—watch out, it just caught a second breeze!
F1
It is gliding past table four, banking left, heading straight for the courtyard fountain basin!
M2
Not the stone water basin! That is washable blue fountain ink, not waterproof paint!
M4
Dive left, {F1}! Grab the dry corner before it lands face down in the water!
F1
Splash... right into the middle of the basin like a giant white paper boat.
M2
Tell me I am dreaming, both of you—where did the pharmacist and the baker go?!
scenes.outro: One gust of wind tangles the rooftop lanterns above and lands twenty-eight blue ink names squarely in the courtyard water basin! See you next time.

scenes.title: Floating in the Basin
scenes.summary: Lifting the soaked poster out of the stone basin, M2 despairs over the blurred blue cloud while M1 and F2 talk him back from panic.
scenes.intro: By the carved stone water basin in the corner of the courtyard, {M2} holds up a dripping pale-blue sheet of paper while {M1} hands him a dry cotton towel and {F2} tries heroically not to laugh. Listen first.
story: M2
Look at Table Three—everyone on {STREET} has merged into one giant blue jellyfish!
M1
Here is a clean towel for your sleeves, boss; at least the water stayed cool.
F2
Honestly, {M2}, abstract watercolour art is very fashionable in cafés right now!
M2
How can twenty-eight neighbours sit down tomorrow without a civilized seating plan?!
M1
Calm down and think—your head still remembers where every single neighbour belongs, right?
M2
Of course I remember every seat, {M1}, but wind blows paper cards off outdoor tables!
F2
He has a point, {M1}; even folded paper place cards flew away ten minutes ago.
M1
Paper flies away only when nobody clips it to something heavy.
M2
Clip it? With what—heavy iron horseshoes on clean white linen napkins?!
M1
Stay right here, drink five sips of mint tea, and let me check my workshop drawer.
F2
First help {M3} rescue those tangled lanterns overhead before the cord knots tight, {M1}!
M1
Lanterns first, windproof seats second—nobody panic on my watch.
scenes.outro: While the blue ink jellyfish dries in the sun, {M1} heads upstairs with a plan to outsmart the Friday wind. See you next time.

scenes.title: Untangling the Lantern Cord
scenes.summary: Back on the upper balcony, M1 and M3 reel in the twisted lantern lines and add wooden spacer loops so the globes stay steady in any breeze.
scenes.intro: Up on the breezy second-floor balcony, {M1} and {M3} work shoulder to shoulder, drawing the two tangled lantern cords carefully back across the wooden railing. Listen first.
story: M3
Pull the left cord gently toward your hand, {M1}—two lanterns hooked their wire handles.
M1
Easy does it... lift the coral globe over the gold one, and they come apart clean.
M3
Zero torn paper! Still, if the wind blows tomorrow evening, these two lines will touch again.
M1
That is why I brought four light cedar dowels drilled at both ends from the cellar.
M3
Wait—wooden spreader bars tied between parallel cords like rigging on a sailing ship?!
M1
My uncle worked harbour boats in his youth; two parallel lines with spacers never twist.
M3
Let me tie this cedar bar halfway—look how steady both cords ride now!
M1
And clip each lantern handle closed with a tiny brass ring so none can jump free.
M3
Architecturally AND nautically brilliant, {M1}—watch them sway gently together in unison!
M1
Not bad for a man who does not own a tablet computer, eh, {M3}?
M3
Every time I work beside you, {M1}, I add another page to my notebook!
M1
Come downstairs now—I have thirty wooden clothespins waiting for {F1} at the front desk.
scenes.outro: Harbour-boat spacer bars keep the rooftop lanterns swaying smoothly together without a single tangle! See you next time.

scenes.title: Twenty-Eight Wooden Clothespins
scenes.summary: At the front desk, M1 pours out sturdy birch clothespins, and F1 numbers them one to twenty-eight in bold pencil to clip onto heavy cloth napkins.
scenes.intro: At the front desk, {M1} unties a canvas drawstring bag and pours three dozen smooth birch-wood clothespins onto the blotter before {F1} and {M2}. Let us listen in first.
story: M2
Wooden laundry clothespins, {M1}?! We are hosting an anniversary tea, not drying bedsheets!
F1
Wait a second, {M2}—look how smooth and clean this natural birch wood is!
M1
Watch what happens when I write Number One in dark carpenter pencil along the flat side.
F1
Pencil on bare wood never smudges in water AND clips tight onto a folded cloth napkin!
M2
Hold on... number on one side, guest name on the other side, clipped to heavy linen?!
F1
And everyone can clip their wooden clothespin onto a saucer or pocket as a keepsake!
M2
{M1}, {F1}—that is charming, rustic, windproof, AND costs zero extra coins!
M1
Plus I kept a full backup seat list written neatly on page forty of my ledger.
F1
Read the names out in order, {M2}, while I letter clothespins one through twenty-eight!
M2
Pin Number One: Our Honoured Mapmaker from Room Eight! Pin Number Two: {F3}!
M1
Look how fast {F1} writes—half the street is already pinned in neat wooden rows.
F1
Take this basket outside and test our windproof tables against the afternoon breeze!
scenes.outro: Humble birch clothespins and dark carpenter pencil turn a soggy poster disaster into windproof courtyard keepsakes! See you next time.

scenes.title: Windproof and Ready
scenes.summary: Just before noon on Saturday, F1, F2, and M3 admire the windproof rooftop lanterns and clipped linen tables—all set for six this evening, until the front-desk telephone rings!
scenes.intro: Late Saturday morning arrives bright and breezy at {SHOW}. At five minutes to twelve, {F1}, {F2}, and {M3} stand under the courtyard tree admiring twenty-four coral-and-gold lanterns swaying steadily from the upper balcony down to the branches. Listen first.
story: F2
Look up at those four lines from the balcony—not one lantern twisted overnight!
M3
And look down at the tables: twenty-eight linen napkins clipped tight with numbered birch pins!
F1
Even {M1} clipped four extra clothespins to the corners of every white tablecloth!
F2
At three this afternoon I bake four berry almond cakes so they are warm by six.
M3
And at four this afternoon {F3} and I finish rehearsing our four-hand piano duet!
F1
Everything is timed to the minute: afternoon prep, five-thirty tea, six sharp arrival!
F2
Knock on wood right now, {F1}, whenever someone says everything is timed to the minute!
M3
What could possibly change at noon? Our guest wrote six this evening in black ink!
F1
Wait—do you two hear the front-desk telephone ringing through the lobby window?
F2
That is a very loud, very urgent Saturday noon ring, {F1}!
M3
Even {M1} just looked up from his paper ledger behind the glass door!
F1
Hold my apron—I had better answer that call before twelve chimes finish!
scenes.outro: Every lantern and clothespin is ready for six this evening—until a noon telephone call flips the Saturday schedule upside down! End of Episode 4—see you in Episode 5!
